Finite-step quadratic Gaussian-cascade transport in Lemma cav:quadratic, and its finite integer-count cavity evaluation and spin-test consequences, independently of the unverified thermodynamic pressure theorem.

definitions.residual: independent centered Gaussian draw at each visit to a leaf, including repeated leaf visits
definitions.coupling: positive rational spectral proportions with integer n*rho_a and the full spectral block compression of cav:coupling

For all finite real square matrix dimensions, the noncommutative factorization, inverse intertwining, resolvent difference, and transported innovation covariance identities hold under the explicit inverse and symmetry hypotheses specified in research/quadratic_cavity/report.md.

Normalized conditional Poisson marking and predictable edge rescaling preserve the unmarked finite Ruelle cascade and sampled branching, leave the common root distribution unchanged, and give the tilted residual kernel independently at every visit; finite backward fractional moments suffice.

For every finite depth k>=1 and dimension d>=0, symmetric K and Loewner decreasing B_0>=...>=B_k=0 with B_0=0 or B_0>0 and B_0^{-1}-K>0, the quadratic Gaussian cascade has the universal joint Gaussian innovation law and integrable expected log normalizer proved in research/quadratic_cavity/report.md, including arbitrary positive semidefinite root covariance and independently redrawn residuals.

Every literal conclusion of Lemma cav:quadratic, build/50-cavity.tex:453-510 in the staged September 25 2026 manuscript, holds under its stated finite-alphabet, symmetric spectral-bound, finite-step quantile, Gaussian-independence, and per-visit residual hypotheses, including the joint terminal-mark representation for every finite number of replicas, p=0, p=1, repeated levels, singular increments, and d=0.

For every finite-step quantile, under all integer-count limiting block-coupling hypotheses of cav:coupling, the normalized logarithmic cavity factor equals ell(h_p)+(1/2)int p*h_p+G_1(p) as in cav:evaluated. The spectral bounds of cav:quadratic alone are not substituted for the block-coupling hypotheses.

Under the same integer-count limiting coupling, every finite-step cavity-spin test equals int phi(p(s))*B_{h_p}(s) ds and the common-level law is unchanged, with separately sampled residuals even at identical leaves. This does not imply B_{h_p}=p or prove the thermodynamic pressure theorem.

For all finite real square matrix dimensions, the noncommutative factorization, inverse intertwining, resolvent difference, and transported innovation covariance identities hold under the explicit inverse and symmetry hypotheses specified in research/quadratic_cavity/report.md.
claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib

namespace QuadraticCavity

section RingIdentities

variable {R : Type*} [Ring R]

theorem ordered_factor (B C K J : R)
    (hC : (1 - C * K) * J = 1) :
    1 - (B - C) * (K * J) = (1 - B * K) * J := by
  calc
    1 - (B - C) * (K * J) =
        (1 - C * K) * J - (B - C) * (K * J) := by rw [hC]
    _ = (1 - B * K) * J := by noncomm_ring

theorem ordered_intertwining (B C K JB JC T : R)
    (hB : JB * (1 - B * K) = 1)
    (hC : (1 - C * K) * JC = 1)
    (hT : (1 - (B - C) * (K * JC)) * T = 1) :
    JC * T = JB := by
  have hCT : ((1 - B * K) * JC) * T = 1 := by
    rw [← ordered_factor B C K JC hC]
    exact hT
  calc
    JC * T = (JB * (1 - B * K)) * (JC * T) := by rw [hB, one_mul]
    _ = JB * (((1 - B * K) * JC) * T) := by simp only [mul_assoc]
    _ = JB := by rw [hCT, mul_one]

theorem left_right_resolvent (C K JC LC : R)
    (hJC : JC * (1 - C * K) = 1)
    (hLC : (1 - K * C) * LC = 1) :
    JC * C = C * LC := by
  calc
    JC * C = JC * C * ((1 - K * C) * LC) := by rw [hLC, mul_one]
    _ = (JC * (1 - C * K)) * C * LC := by noncomm_ring
    _ = C * LC := by rw [hJC, one_mul]

theorem ordered_resolvent_difference (B C K JB JC LC : R)
    (hB : JB * (1 - B * K) = 1)
    (hJC : JC * (1 - C * K) = 1)
    (hLC : (1 - K * C) * LC = 1) :
    JB * B - JC * C = JB * (B - C) * LC := by
  rw [left_right_resolvent C K JC LC hJC hLC]
  calc
    JB * B - C * LC =
        JB * B * ((1 - K * C) * LC) -
          (JB * (1 - B * K)) * C * LC := by
      rw [hB, hLC, mul_one, one_mul]
    _ = JB * (B - C) * LC := by noncomm_ring

end RingIdentities

section MatrixIdentities

variable {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

theorem transpose_right_inverse (C K J : Matrix n n ℝ)
    (hC : C.transpose = C) (hK : K.transpose = K)
    (hJ : J * (1 - C * K) = 1) :
    (1 - K * C) * J.transpose = 1 := by
  have h := congrArg Matrix.transpose hJ
  simpa only [Matrix.transpose_mul, Matrix.transpose_sub,
    Matrix.transpose_one, hC, hK] using h

theorem matrix_resolvent_difference (B C K JB JC : Matrix n n ℝ)
    (hC : C.transpose = C) (hK : K.transpose = K)
    (hJB : JB * (1 - B * K) = 1)
    (hJC : JC * (1 - C * K) = 1) :
    JB * B - JC * C = JB * (B - C) * JC.transpose := by
  exact ordered_resolvent_difference B C K JB JC JC.transpose hJB hJC
    (transpose_right_inverse C K JC hC hK hJC)

theorem innovation_covariance (JB JC T S : Matrix n n ℝ)
    (hJT : JC * T = JB) :
    JC * (T * S) * JC.transpose = JB * S * JC.transpose := by
  calc
    JC * (T * S) * JC.transpose =
        (JC * T) * S * JC.transpose := by simp only [mul_assoc]
    _ = JB * S * JC.transpose := by rw [hJT]

theorem scaled_covariance_difference (B C K JB JC S : Matrix n n ℝ)
    (a : ℝ)
    (hC : C.transpose = C) (hK : K.transpose = K)
    (hJB : JB * (1 - B * K) = 1)
    (hJC : JC * (1 - C * K) = 1)
    (hDelta : B - C = a • S) :
    JB * B - JC * C = a • (JB * S * JC.transpose) := by
  calc
    JB * B - JC * C = JB * (B - C) * JC.transpose :=
      matrix_resolvent_difference B C K JB JC hC hK hJB hJC
    _ = JB * (a • S) * JC.transpose := by rw [hDelta]
    _ = a • (JB * S * JC.transpose) := by
      simp only [mul_smul_comm, smul_mul_assoc]

end MatrixIdentities

end QuadraticCavity

claims.natural_statement: Normalized conditional Poisson marking and predictable edge rescaling preserve the unmarked finite Ruelle cascade and sampled branching, leave the common root distribution unchanged, and give the tilted residual kernel independently at every visit; finite backward fractional moments suffice.

external_assumptions.statement: For 0<x<1, a Poisson process on (0,infinity) times a Polish mark space with intensity x*v^(-x-1)dv tensor mu, and positive measurable g with finite integral g^x dmu, the transformation (v,y) to (v*g(y),y) yields intensity x*u^(-x-1)du tensor g(y)^x*mu(dy). Taking integral g^x dmu=1 preserves the unmarked process and gives the normalized tilted conditional mark law.
external_assumptions.source: Bolthausen and Sznitman (1998), primary PDF research/quadratic_cavity/literature/BS1998.pdf, passage transcribed in BS_A2_excerpt.txt; the same mapping is reproved in report.md.

routes.retired_because: The determinant fixes a scalar normalization but cannot identify off-diagonal joint terminal-mark covariances, the quenched common root, or independent per-visit residuals.
